# shift-router

> It's a CTO for the work that matters, an engineer for the workload. An LLM judge picks the right role per turn; multi-model fallback chains keep you running; complex tasks are orchestrated by a Smart CTO that delegates to Fast subagents. Two editions: pi-coding-agent and DeepSeek Harness.

## About

shift-router is a family of task-level model routers — **pi-shift-router** (v1.3.0, pi-coding-agent extension) and **dsh-shift-router** (v0.5.0, DeepSeek Harness plugin). Both classify every turn and route between two roles:

- **Fast = Engineer** — handles the workload: writes code, runs tests, fixes bugs, follows established patterns. For routine, well-defined, low-stakes work.
- **Smart = CTO** — for the work that matters: sets direction, corrects course, reviews results, and takes on the hard problems itself — architecture, design review, security audit, multi-step planning, irrecoverable actions.

A small LLM Judge (the fast-tier model itself, JSON mode) classifies each turn as fast or smart. Upgrades are immediate; downgrades need a sustained trend (fast votes ≥ 60% of the last 5 turns). On 429/5xx, the failing model enters exponential-backoff cooldown — 5xx starts at 1m (1m → 4m → 16m → 1h → 4h… capped 6h), while a failover-worthy 4xx (429/quota) starts at 16m — and the next healthy model in the same tier takes over.

**Task-level orchestration (v1.3.0):** when the Judge says a task is complex and orchestration is in auto mode (default), the Smart tier runs as a CTO that plans the work, delegates implementation to Fast engineer subagents (fresh context, model pinned from the Fast tier), reviews each result, and iterates until clean. Simple tasks never orchestrate. Hard caps: maxRounds 3, escalationThreshold 2. Every orchestrated turn ends with an **acceptance audit** (v1.3.0): deterministic checks always run (every worker reported back, a CTO summary is present, no silent hard-cap hit), plus an optional fast-tier LLM audit that checks grounding, goal alignment, and delivered quality — findings surface as console.warn + toast and `/router status → Last audit`. Re-delegations must carry a structured failure report (convergence protocol). Requires pi-subagents; without it, complex tasks run directly on Smart (no crash, no deadlock).

## The family

| | pi-shift-router | dsh-shift-router |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | pi-coding-agent extension | DeepSeek Harness plugin |
| Version | v1.3.0 | v0.5.0 |
| Install | `pi install npm:pi-shift-router` | `git clone …/dsh-shift-router && npm install && npm run build` + `dsh plugin --profile web add <path>` |
| Config | `/router config` wizard | GUI settings panel + `/router config` commands |
| Capabilities | same LLM Judge, cache-aware routing, failover, orchestration, cost telemetry | same |
| Tests | 369 unit tests | 109 unit tests + credential-free headless e2e |

## Key facts

- Runtime: Node.js ≥ 24 (pi), Node.js ≥ 22 (DSH)
- Dependencies: zero runtime deps (pure TypeScript)
- License: MIT
- Author: green-dalii
- Repositories: https://github.com/green-dalii/pi-shift-router · https://github.com/green-dalii/dsh-shift-router
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-shift-router

## Install (pi)

```bash
pi install npm:pi-shift-router
```

Registers in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and auto-loads on the next pi launch.

Optional (recommended) for orchestration:

```bash
pi install npm:pi-subagents
```

## Install (DeepSeek Harness)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/green-dalii/dsh-shift-router.git
cd dsh-shift-router
npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-shift-router
```

The bundle's cordis.patch.yml inserts the plugin into any profile that lists it. Tier models come from the settings panel or the patch row. Configuration is editable live (GUI panel + `/router config`; code changes still need a restart).

## Configure

Inside pi, run `/router config` and pick one Fast + one Smart model. Save to user or project scope. On DSH, edit the `shift-router` settings namespace in the GUI or via `/router config set`.

## Verify

`/router status` shows your tiers, orchestration mode, session stats, cost telemetry, and config; the next turn triggers the first Judge call.

## Commands

- `/router status` / `/router stats` — show tiers, orchestration mode, cost telemetry, stats, config
- `/router on` / `/router off` — enable / disable routing
- `/router config` — launch the configuration wizard (pi) / show effective config (DSH)
- `/router quiet` — toggle inline toast notifications
- `/router verbose` — toggle verbose console logging
- `/router orchestrate auto|off` — task-level orchestration on (default) or plain two-tier routing
- `/route-force <tier>` — pin Smart or Fast for the next turn
- `/route-force <provider>/<model>` — pin a specific model for the next turn
- `/route-force auto` — clear manual override

`/router status` reports cost telemetry: per-tier spend (USD + calls) and a savings baseline — what the session would have cost if every turn ran on your Smart model (i.e. no router). Example: `Spend: fast $0.045 (9 calls) · smart $0.42 (3 calls) · total $0.465; baseline $3.21; saved $2.74`.

## Configuration

Two-layer config (pi): user (`~/.pi/agent/pi-shift-router.json`) + project (`<cwd>/.pi/pi-shift-router.json`). Project wins on conflict. On DSH, config lives in the `shift-router` settings namespace (same store for GUI and commands).

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "tiers": {
    "fast":  { "models": [
      { "provider": "deepseek", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "priority": 1 },
      { "provider": "kimi",     "model": "kimi-k3",          "priority": 2 }
    ] },
    "smart": { "models": [{ "provider": "kimi", "model": "kimi-k3", "priority": 1 }] }
  },
  "routing": { "mode": "auto", "judgeTimeout": 5000, "window": { "size": 5, "threshold": 0.6 } },
  "orchestration": { "mode": "auto", "maxRounds": 3, "escalationThreshold": 2 },
  "ux": { "quietMode": false, "statusBar": true, "inlineToast": true, "routerLogVerbose": false }
}
```

## FAQ

- **What if I don't configure any models?** Both tiers start empty. The router is a no-op; pi/DSH uses its default model. Run `/router config`.
- **Does the Judge add noticeable latency?** A few thousand tokens at Fast-tier pricing; end-to-end classification typically 200ms–2s. Status bar shows `🧭 judging…`.
- **What if my primary model 429s or times out?** Exponential-backoff cooldown — 5xx from 1m, failover-worthy 4xx (429/quota) from 16m, capped at 6h; next healthy model in the same tier takes over. A 2xx response clears the cooldown.
- **What is task-level orchestration?** A smart verdict on a complex task makes the Smart tier act as CTO: plan → delegate to Fast subagents → review → iterate → accept. `/router orchestrate off` disables it. Needs pi-subagents (pi) / deployment-pinned worker model (DSH).
- **Are DSH subagents routed?** No — subagents keep their pinned model; only top-level agents are routed.
- **Does this work across different providers?** Yes — each tier is an ordered list of `{provider, model, priority}` pairs.
- **Can I monitor cost?** Yes — `/router status` reports per-tier spend and a savings baseline vs. running everything on Smart.
